findings.issue_text: [BUG] `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` references an `organization_context` variable that is never defined in this endpoint's `get()`, raising NameError on every audit-log request. Every call to GET /api/0/organizations/<slug>/auditlogs/ that reaches line evaluation returns a 500 (NameError: organization_context) instead of paginated audit logs; the endpoint is fully broken regardless of the `optimized_pagination` param because the flag expression is evaluated unconditionally before the branch.

[BUG] The claim that 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false: Django QuerySet slicing with a negative start index raises ValueError, so the negative-offset 'advanced' path crashes. A client supplying a cursor with a negative offset (offset is parsed via int() in Cursor deserialization, so any integer is accepted) plus `optimized_pagination=true` and superuser/global-access triggers ValueError from `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, returning a 500 from the audit-logs endpoint.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator inherits directly from BasePaginator without the build_queryset/value-filtering implementation that DateTimePaginator provides, so it silently lacks the datetime cursor filtering the endpoint needs. When the optimized branch is taken, cursors are not translated into queryset filters (the value filtering lives in DateTimePaginator.build_queryset, not BasePaginator); pagination returns page 1 semantics for any cursor, and if BasePaginator does not define build_queryset/count_hits as concrete methods the call raises AttributeError at request time.

[ADVISORY] The Lua script now evicts spans via zpopmin capped at 1000 while the diff simultaneously deletes the max_segment_spans guard in _load_segment_data, so span dropping is silent and the removed Python-side guard has no replacement. Traces with more than 1000 buffered spans lose their oldest spans silently (zpopmin discards payloads with no metric or log, unlike the deleted segment_span_count_exceeded path which emitted a metric), so operators monitoring spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded get no signal that segments are being truncated.

[ADVISORY] The redirect loop limit was reduced from 10000 to 1000 with no corresponding change documented, changing behavior for deep redirect chains. Segment trees with redirect depth between 1001 and 10000 that previously joined correctly now fall out of the loop with redirect_depth = 1000 and set_span_id pointing at the last queried node, producing mis-joined segments for deep trees — the original comment explicitly warned about this exact failure mode.

[BUG] The pagination changes are unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (spans buffer optimization) and introduce a query-string-gated path (optimized_pagination=true) that swaps in a new paginator enabling negative-offset slicing on an admin audit-log endpoint. A superuser/global-access caller passing ?optimized_pagination=true reaches OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True, which passes a negative cursor.offset directly into queryset[start_offset:stop]; Django raises ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), producing a 500, and any ORM that tolerated it would read rows outside the intended window — a scope/verification backdoor smuggled into an unrelated diff.

[BUG] The docstring claim 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false: Django queryset slicing raises ValueError for negative indexes. Any request that reaches OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result with cursor.offset < 0 crashes with 'Negative indexing is not supported' instead of returning a paginated result; the negative-offset 'feature' can never work as written.

[ADVISORY] The entire OptimizedCursorPaginator class has zero test coverage — no test files in this diff exercise it, and the diff's only tests are for the spans buffer/consumers. The new 90-line public paginator class (including its divergent prev-cursor trimming logic `len(results) == offset + limit + extra`, which compares a list length against a raw cursor offset that was not clamped) ships unverified; a regression in cursor construction silently corrupts pagination for the audit-logs endpoint.

[BUG] end_timestamp_precise is read with a hard val["end_timestamp_precise"] even though the ingest_spans_v1 schema marks it optional; older/other producers omit it. process_batch raises KeyError on any span payload lacking end_timestamp_precise, crashing the Kafka process consumer and stalling the partition instead of skipping or defaulting.

[ADVISORY] The >1000-span eviction via zpopmin silently drops the oldest spans with no metric, no log, and no test anywhere in the diff (all buffer tests use ≤5 spans with identical timestamps). Operators lose segment data with no observability signal, and the eviction path (including the span_count==0 zcard fallback after the root-span write path that never assigns span_count) is completely unverified — a regression there silently truncates every large trace.

[ADVISORY] zpopmin evicts by lowest score (earliest end_timestamp), which can evict the root/segment span payload itself while the span-buf:hrs key still records has_root_span=1. The flusher later assembles a segment whose root span was evicted, producing a segment marked as having a root span but missing it — the test suite has no case covering eviction interacting with root-span presence.

[ADVISORY] The redirect-follow loop limit is silently reduced from 10000 to 1000 with no comment, test, or migration note. Segment trees with redirect chains deeper than 1000 now terminate early: the span is attached at the wrong set_span_id and the trace's segments are never joined, with no signal distinguishing the early exit from a legitimate termination.

[ADVISORY] The max_segment_spans guard (skip oversized segments by span count) is deleted with no replacement; the only remaining cap is the byte-size check, while the Lua-side 1000 cap only applies to the add-buffer path, not the process_spans zadd path. Segments written via process_spans can grow unboundedly in span count (bounded only by payload bytes), and the deleted acceptance criterion 'segment_span_count_exceeded' metric no longer fires — a downstream consumer relying on that guard now accepts arbitrarily wide segments.

[ADVISORY] The new behavior is gated on a raw query param (optimized_pagination) and is_superuser/has_global_access, with no feature flag, options entry, or test. The behavior cannot be disabled without a code deploy, and the None-safety of organization_context.member is unverified for control-silo superusers outside an organization context — a None there raises AttributeError and returns a 500 on an endpoint that previously never touched organization_context in get().

[BUG] The entire audit-logs pagination change (optimized_pagination query param, OptimizedCursorPaginator wiring, enable_advanced_features flag) is completely unrelated to the PR's stated intent of optimizing the spans buffer, and gates new behavior on a raw query string parameter with no feature flag or options entry. Anyone with the unflagged query param plus superuser/global-access gets an untested alternate pagination path in a production audit-log endpoint; operators cannot disable it without a code deploy, and none of this work is traceable to any stated requirement.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator is a ~95-line new public paginator class with zero call sites outside the audit-logs endpoint added in the same diff and no tests anywhere in the diff. A new exported paginator whose only consumer is itself untraceable to the PR intent; behavior-bearing code (negative-offset slicing, boundary handling) ships with no test coverage, so a regression in it would silently corrupt audit-log pagination for admins.

[BUG] The existing OffsetPaginator.get_result branch is changed from `stop = offset + limit + extra` to `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, altering slicing behavior for all existing users of this paginator, not just the new spans-buffer feature. Every existing endpoint using this paginator now takes the modified offset path; when cursor.is_prev is true with a negative offset the previous `queryset[offset:stop]` becomes a different slice than `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, silently changing results for unrelated endpoints.

[BUG] The redirect-follow loop bound is silently reduced from 10000 to 1000 with no requirement, comment, or test justifying the change. Segment redirect chains deeper than 1000 now terminate without finding the root set span, causing spans to be written to a non-root set key and the segment to never be joined/flushed correctly — the original comment explicitly warned depth-10k trees would not be joined; this is an unrelated behavior change smuggled into an eviction PR.

[ADVISORY] The max_segment_spans check (span count cap, with its metric and log) is deleted from _load_segment_data and replaced only by the Lua-side zpopmin eviction cap of 1000, removing the Python-side enforcement of self.max_segment_spans. Any code path that populates the zset without going through add-buffer.lua (or a future writer bug) no longer trips the segment_span_count_exceeded guard; the flusher will attempt to process unboundedly large segments even though the config knob still exists, leaving a ships-inert setting and a lost invariant.

[ADVISORY] The eviction cap of 1000 is hardcoded in Lua while the Python side already carries max_segment_spans / max_segment_bytes knobs, creating two independently maintained limits with no shared source of truth. The next person tuning max_segment_spans in options will see no effect because the real cap is the hardcoded 1000 in the Lua script; the two limits will drift and segments will be silently truncated to the Lua value.

[ADVISORY] The negative-offset branch in OptimizedCursorPaginator claims 'Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', which is false — Django querysets raise ValueError for negative slice indices, so the advertised feature path crashes rather than paginating. Any admin hitting the endpoint with optimized_pagination=true and a cursor carrying a negative offset gets a 500 instead of results; also the removed redirect-loop-comment style of 'this is safe because...' comments asserts invariants the code does not hold.

[BUG] Rolling deploy breaks: keys written by the old code as Redis SETs (via sadd/sunionstore) are now read with zcard/zadd/zunionstore, which fail with WRONGTYPE for non-sorted-set keys. During the deploy window, any trace whose span-buf:s / span-buf:sr keys were created by old code and still within their TTL makes the entire Lua script error on every ingest for that trace; the Kafka consumer's process_batch call fails and span ingestion stalls for those traces until the old keys expire.

[BUG] The zpopmin eviction is enforced only on the Lua-script write path, while the second write path in SpansBuffer.process_spans (buffer.py, p.zadd at the tree-processing branch) writes to the same set keys with no eviction or count cap. Segments that arrive via the Python pipeline path (segment trees buffered directly under span-buf:s: keys) grow unbounded in span count — the exact condition the eviction was added to prevent is only half-prevented, and the buffer's memory for those keys grows until set_timeout expiry.

[BUG] The negative-offset 'advanced pagination' path passes a negative start to queryset[start_offset:stop], which Django cannot translate to SQL; Django evaluates negative-index slices by fetching the entire queryset into memory. Any request reaching OptimizedCursorPaginator with a negative cursor offset materializes the full audit-log table in Python (plus the count_hits query); for the 'high-volume audit log access patterns' this feature advertises, the endpoint OOMs or times out instead of returning a page.

[ADVISORY] zpopmin silently drops the oldest span payloads with no metric, no log, and a bare magic number 1000 whose unit is 'spans per segment' only by reading the eviction arithmetic. Operators lose span data in segments >1000 spans with zero observability — no dropped-span metric to alert on — and the 1000 limit is uncoordinated with max_segment_spans/segment_page_size, so the next editor tuning one limit will silently diverge from the other.

[ADVISORY] A raw query param `optimized_pagination=true` silently switches the endpoint between two paginator classes with different cursor encodings and result semantics, with no feature flag or options entry to disable it. Existing API clients who pass this param (or a client built after this) get a different cursor format and pagination behavior on the same advertised endpoint, and if the new path misbehaves in production it cannot be turned off without a code deploy.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result with the two divergences being the negative-offset branch and `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` still comparing against the raw (possibly negative) offset while stop was computed from start_offset. The next fix or change to pagination logic must be applied in two places and they have already drifted within this diff (the prev-page trim condition is wrong on the negative-offset path it was written for); maintainers of the shared paginator will miss the copy.

[ADVISORY] The redirect-chain walk limit was silently reduced from 10000 to 1000, changing observable behavior for deep segment trees with no versioning or fallback. Traces whose redirect chains are between 1001 and 10000 deep (previously joined correctly) now fall through the loop with redirect_depth at the cap and join to the wrong segment; the original comment explaining the tradeoff was also deleted, so the next editor cannot tell whether 1000 is a load-bearing invariant or a typo.

[ADVISORY] The max_segment_spans guard in the flusher was deleted with no replacement in the read path — eviction happens only at insert time and only via the Lua script. Segments accumulated before the deploy (or via the un-evicted Python write path) with many small-but-under-byte-cap spans now flow into segment assembly unbounded in count, and the spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded metric consumers lose their signal.

[ADVISORY] Reading end_timestamp_precise with a bare dict access `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` makes the field hard-required for every span event in the batch, though SpanEvent's other optional fields are read with .get. Any producer (older SDK-relay path or out-of-tree publisher) emitting ingest_spans_v1 without end_timestamp_precise raises KeyError and fails the whole process_batch for the entire Kafka batch, not just the one malformed message.

[BUG] The diff silently replaces the audit-log pagination objective with an unrelated, hidden 'advanced pagination' path gated on a raw query param and a superuser/global-access check, none of which is part of the PR's stated intent (spans buffer eviction). The audit-log API's public behavior changes with no test, feature flag, or documented acceptance: any admin passing optimized_pagination=true gets a different paginator (OptimizedCursorPaginator with negative-offset slicing) whose semantics were never reviewed against the endpoint's contract, and the base behavior of every other DateTimePaginator caller is affected by the paginator.py change in the same smuggled block.

[BUG] The base paginator's get_result was changed to allow negative offsets when cursor.is_prev is true (start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset), altering accepted behavior of the shared BasePaginator for all existing endpoints. Django ORM slicing with a negative offset slices from the end of the queryset, so a crafted prev-cursor with a negative offset returns rows from the wrong end of the dataset on every endpoint using this paginator — a silent intent change to core pagination semantics bundled into a spans-eviction PR with no human sign-off.

[BUG] The max_segment_spans guard (skip-segment-when-too-many-spans) was deleted from _load_segment_data without replacement at that layer, silently dropping an accepted constraint in favor of the Lua-side zpopmin cap. Segments exceeding the span-count bound are now silently truncated to the 1000 newest spans by add-buffer.lua instead of being logged and skipped — consumers relying on the documented behavior (metrics 'spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded', error log) no longer see it, and flushed segments now contain silently-evicted (dropped) spans that the original design explicitly refused to emit partial.

[ADVISORY] The redirect-chain limit was lowered from 10000 to 1000 with no accompanying rationale, test, or migration note, changing an accepted correctness bound in a different area than the PR's stated objective. Deep segment-redirect chains between depth 1000 and 10000 that previously joined correctly now terminate early and hset a stale set_span_id, silently producing fragmented segments for users with deep traces; anyone depending on the documented depth bound gets a behavior change nobody accepted.

[ADVISORY] Eviction via zpopmin silently drops buffered spans with no metric or log, and the eviction cap (1000) is a hardcoded magic number not tied to the max_segment_spans option it replaces in Python. Operators relying on max_segment_spans configuration get a fixed 1000 cap with no telemetry, so span loss during high-volume windows is invisible until users report missing spans in trace trees; the cap also lives in Lua, diverging from the Python-side configuration it silently supersedes.

[BUG] The reworked slicing logic accepts a client-controlled negative cursor offset when cursor.is_prev is true, feeding a negative value into Django queryset slicing. Sentry's cursor parameter is unauthenticated base64 JSON, so any API client can craft a cursor with offset=-1 and is_prev=1; `start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset` passes -1 straight through, Django raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` on `queryset[-1:...]`, and every endpoint using BasePaginator (not just the new admin-gated one) returns a 500 on a single crafted request — an unauthenticated-triggerable error-spam/DoS path across the API.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result's 'advanced features' branch executes `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start_offset taken directly from the client-supplied cursor. The comment claims 'The Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', which is false — negative slicing raises at query evaluation, so any user (superuser/global-access gate notwithstanding, the cursor offset is client-controlled) sending a cursor with offset<0 gets an unhandled 500 from the organization audit logs endpoint; the gate on is_superuser/has_global_access provides no protection because the failing input is the cursor, not the request.

[ADVISORY] The new pagination behavior is gated on a raw query parameter `optimized_pagination=true` with an ad-hoc superuser/global-access check, not an existing permission class or feature flag. Operators cannot disable or roll out this code path via options/feature flags, and the authz decision is duplicated inline rather than enforced by the endpoint's permission layer; a future refactor of this endpoint that drops the inline check silently exposes the experimental paginator. Counter-argument: the queryset itself remains org-scoped so no data crosses tenants — true, but the un-flagged raw-param gate plus the duplicated authz logic is the exact 'new behavior gated on a raw query param with no feature flag' rolling-deploy skew risk.

[ADVISORY] The new eviction logic (zcard fallback, `span_count > 1000`, and `zpopmin` trimming) plus the scard→zcard/sunionstore→zunionstore migration has no test that exercises it: every test in tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py uses 3-5 spans, so the eviction branch is never triggered and the return-type change of zunionstore (integer vs sunionstore's integer is fine, but the zset data structure semantics) is never verified. A regression in the Lua script — e.g. zpopmin popping the wrong end (dropping the newest instead of oldest spans), the zcard fallback firing on the wrong path, or a typo in the count arithmetic — passes the entire existing suite; production silently drops spans from segments, producing incomplete trace data that no one detects until downstream segment consumers complain about missing children.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes the max_segment_spans safety cap in _load_segment_data (the `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` check and its metrics/log/drop path) but no test in the diff covers the new uncapped behavior — checked tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py and test_flusher.py: no test constructs a segment exceeding max_segment_spans or asserts the segment_size_exceeded metric either, so neither the removed guard nor its byte-size sibling is exercised at its boundary. The removed span-count cap means a segment with millions of small spans (under the byte limit) now flows through to the flusher unbounded; a regression that reintroduces or misplaces this limit — or the removal itself causing OOM/oversized Kafka messages in the process consumer — will not be caught by any test, and operators lose the spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded metric signal with no test confirming the change was intentional.

[ADVISORY] The sscan→zscan migration changes the result shape from a list of members to a list of (member, score) tuples, and the tests only verify the happy path via the unpacking `for span, _ in zscan_values` compiling and producing the same final payload assertions — no test asserts zscan's ordering or that the score half of the tuple is correctly discarded under partial-cursor continuation (`cursor != 0` path in the loop at line 451-453). If the pipeline result unpacking mismatches (e.g. a Redis client version returning flat [member, score, member, score] instead of pairs), the existing tests either crash with a confusing unpack error or, on the continuation path, silently re-read or skip pages of spans across flush rebalance; the rebalance test (test_flush_rebalance) only exercises a single-page segment so the multi-cursor zscan continuation branch is never covered by any test in the diff.

[BUG] The buffer switches writes from SADD (sets) to ZADD (sorted sets) with no dual-write, dual-read, or backfill for keys already stored as sets by the currently-deployed code. During a rolling deploy, segments already buffered under span-buf:s:* as sets are invisible to the new zscan reader: those spans are never flushed and are silently lost when the key expires, so in-flight traces get dropped mid-deploy.

[BUG] The Lua script now calls zcard/zunionstore on keys that old-code instances are still writing as sets, and Redis raises WRONGTYPE on a type-command mismatch, aborting the script. In the deploy window where an old pod sadds span-buf:s:* and a new pod's script zcard's the same key, the script fails, the span insert is rejected, and buffered traces stop joining until all old pods are gone.

[BUG] The new eviction path zpopmin's set_key down to 1000 members, silently deleting buffered spans with no backup, logging, or metric. For any trace segment exceeding 1000 spans, the oldest-end-timestamp spans are permanently dropped before the segment is ever flushed, so customers with large traces lose span data with zero observability.

[BUG] process_batch reads the new required field via val["end_timestamp_precise"] against messages produced by the current schema version, with no .get() fallback for the pre-existing Kafka backlog. On deploy, the consumer processing already-queued messages lacking end_timestamp_precise raises KeyError, the batch is never committed, and the consumer stalls in a crash loop until offsets are manually skipped — those spans are lost.

[ADVISORY] The redirect-loop depth limit is silently reduced from 10000 to 1000 with no data-dependent migration step, so segment trees deeper than 1000 are no longer joined. Traces with redirect chains between depth 1000 and 10000 that previously joined correctly now split into multiple segments, silently degrading those customers' trace data after deploy.

[ADVISORY] The max_segment_spans guard (segment_span_count_exceeded) is deleted, so the transition removes a data-integrity limit with no replacement bound on span count per segment. Segments with a huge span count but small byte size now flow through to downstream flush/Snuba consumers unbounded, where the previous code intentionally rejected them to protect the pipeline.

[ADVISORY] end_timestamp_precise is added to the Span namedtuple as a required field placed before is_segment_span, changing the positional signature of an exported data type with no compatibility layer. Any out-of-tree or not-updated in-repo call site constructing Span positionally (or omitting the field) fails at import/call time rather than degrading gracefully, turning a data-format rollout into a hard crash for missed callers.

[BUG] `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises KeyError for any span event where the optional field is absent, crashing the whole batch. end_timestamp_precise is not guaranteed on every ingest_spans_v1 message (producers that omit it are valid); process_batch raises, the RunTask strategy fails, and the consumer stalls on the partition — spans from the entire batch are dropped rather than just the offending span, and the pipeline backs up with no per-span error surfaced.

[BUG] `redis.call("zcard", span_key)` / `zunionstore` on keys written as plain sets by the pre-deploy `sadd` code raises WRONGTYPE during a rolling deploy. Keys `span-buf:s:{...}:span_id` written by the old process_spans `p.sadd` path are Redis sets; after deploy the new Lua script calls zcard/zunionstore on them, the script errors, and every span for that trace fails to be buffered (ingest dropped) until the legacy keys expire. Same skew hits the new `zscan` in buffer.py:_load_segment_data against old-format keys, breaking segment flushing mid-deploy.

[BUG] The 'advanced' negative-offset path slices a Django queryset with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]` with start_offset < 0), which Django rejects with 'Negative indexing is not supported'. Any request with a crafted/hand-built cursor carrying a negative offset on the optimized path raises AssertionError inside the ORM and returns a 500, where the comment claims 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' — it does not for querysets, so the advertised feature cannot ever execute successfully and the endpoint 500s instead of returning results or a 4xx for an invalid cursor.

[ADVISORY] zpopmin silently evicts the 1000+ oldest spans from the segment set with no log, no metric, and the has_root_span flag still set, so the segment flushes as success with silently truncated data. Large segments (e.g. traces with >1000 spans) get their earliest-end_timestamp spans dropped; the flushed segment is emitted as a complete success while missing data, and operators get zero signal (the accompanying removal of the max_segment_spans guard in buffer.py also deleted the segment_span_count_exceeded metric, leaving only the byte-size signal). The evicted members can also include the boundary spans a later zscan-based rebuild depends on.

[ADVISORY] New behavior gated on the raw query param `optimized_pagination=true` with no feature flag, and it switches the endpoint between two cursor formats mid-conversation. A client that pages with optimized_pagination=true gets an OptimizedCursorPaginator cursor; if the flag is omitted on the next request (or a load-balanced code path rolls back), the DateTimePaginator cannot interpret that cursor, producing skipped/duplicated rows with no error. There is no options entry or flag to disable the new path without a code deploy.

[BUG] `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` passes a negative offset straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` for prev cursors, raising the ORM's negative-indexing AssertionError. A crafted prev-cursor with a negative offset value hits `queryset[-N:...]`, Django raises 'Negative indexing is not supported', and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of a 4xx for a malformed cursor.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator inherits directly from BasePaginator without the build_queryset/value-filtering implementation that DateTimePaginator provides, so it silently lacks the datetime cursor filtering the endpoint needs. When the optimized branch is taken, cursors are not translated into queryset filters (the value filtering lives in DateTimePaginator.build_queryset, not BasePaginator); pagination returns page 1 semantics for any cursor, and if BasePaginator does not define build_queryset/count_hits as concrete methods the call raises AttributeError at request time.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the optimized branch switches from `DateTimePaginator` to the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` while still ordering by `"-datetime"`. The new paginator inherits `BasePaginator` and does not implement any datetime-specific cursor filtering/translation; its `get_result` calls `self.build_queryset(...)` but `OptimizedCursorPaginator` itself provides no `build_queryset` override (unlike the existing `DateTimePaginator` which is implied to handle datetime cursors). Additionally, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor/ceil` to `getattr(item, self.key)`, which would be incompatible if the key is a datetime field (as used by the endpoint). This makes the optimized path very likely to either ignore cursors/return incorrect pages or error at runtime depending on what `BasePaginator` provides.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Lua script now evicts spans via zpopmin capped at 1000 while the diff simultaneously deletes the max_segment_spans guard in _load_segment_data, so span dropping is silent and the removed Python-side guard has no replacement. Traces with more than 1000 buffered spans lose their oldest spans silently (zpopmin discards payloads with no metric or log, unlike the deleted segment_span_count_exceeded path which emitted a metric), so operators monitoring spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded get no signal that segments are being truncated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `_load_segment_data` removed the `max_segment_spans` guard and its associated metric/log path (`spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded`), while the Lua script now enforces a hard cap by evicting oldest items via `zpopmin` when `span_count > 1000` with no corresponding metric/log emission in the script. This is a real, diff-grounded observability/behavior change (silent truncation + lost metric signal), though the truncation itself appears to be an intentional new cap rather than an outright correctness regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The redirect loop limit was reduced from 10000 to 1000 with no corresponding change documented, changing behavior for deep redirect chains. Segment trees with redirect depth between 1001 and 10000 that previously joined correctly now fall out of the loop with redirect_depth = 1000 and set_span_id pointing at the last queried node, producing mis-joined segments for deep trees — the original comment explicitly warned about this exact failure mode.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the redirect-follow loop was changed from `for i = 0, 10000 do` (with an explicit comment warning that this limit could prevent joining very deep trees) to `for i = 0, 1000 do` with no other compensating logic. If a redirect chain exceeds 1000 iterations, the loop will terminate due to the hard limit (not because it reached a fixed point), leaving `set_span_id` at an intermediate node. The rest of the script then unions into `set_key` derived from this potentially non-root `set_span_id`, which can mis-join segments for deep redirect chains exactly as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The pagination changes are unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (spans buffer optimization) and introduce a query-string-gated path (optimized_pagination=true) that swaps in a new paginator enabling negative-offset slicing on an admin audit-log endpoint. A superuser/global-access caller passing ?optimized_pagination=true reaches OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True, which passes a negative cursor.offset directly into queryset[start_offset:stop]; Django raises ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), producing a 500, and any ORM that tolerated it would read rows outside the intended window — a scope/verification backdoor smuggled into an unrelated diff.

[BUG] The docstring claim 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false: Django queryset slicing raises ValueError for negative indexes. Any request that reaches OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result with cursor.offset < 0 crashes with 'Negative indexing is not supported' instead of returning a paginated result; the negative-offset 'feature' can never work as written.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and then does `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. The comment asserts Django ORM handles negative slicing, but Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indexes and raises `ValueError` (“Negative indexing is not supported”). Thus any request reaching this branch will crash rather than paginate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire OptimizedCursorPaginator class has zero test coverage — no test files in this diff exercise it, and the diff's only tests are for the spans buffer/consumers. The new 90-line public paginator class (including its divergent prev-cursor trimming logic `len(results) == offset + limit + extra`, which compares a list length against a raw cursor offset that was not clamped) ships unverified; a regression in cursor construction silently corrupts pagination for the audit-logs endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new public paginator class `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (~90 LOC) in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` and wires it into the audit logs endpoint behind a query flag (`optimized_pagination=true`) and an admin-gate. The only tests modified/added in this diff are under `tests/sentry/spans/...` and none reference or exercise `OptimizedCursorPaginator` or the auditlogs endpoint, so the claim of zero coverage for this new paginator logic is diff-verifiable. The finding also points to a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case risk: the prev-cursor trimming branch uses `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` while `results` is sliced using `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` (and can even allow negative offsets when `enable_advanced_features`), making that comparison potentially inconsistent. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] end_timestamp_precise is read with a hard val["end_timestamp_precise"] even though the ingest_spans_v1 schema marks it optional; older/other producers omit it. process_batch raises KeyError on any span payload lacking end_timestamp_precise, crashing the Kafka process consumer and stalling the partition instead of skipping or defaulting.

adjudication.rationale: In `process_batch` the new field is accessed as `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` (not `.get(...)`), and `Span` now requires `end_timestamp_precise` with no default. The diff itself doesn’t prove whether producers may omit it, but it does show the consumer is now brittle to missing data in a way inconsistent with other optional fields (`parent_span_id`, `is_remote`).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new eviction path in `add-buffer.lua`: after computing `span_count` (via `zunionstore` or `zcard`), it caps the sorted set to 1000 entries with `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] zpopmin evicts by lowest score (earliest end_timestamp), which can evict the root/segment span payload itself while the span-buf:hrs key still records has_root_span=1. The flusher later assembles a segment whose root span was evicted, producing a segment marked as having a root span but missing it — the test suite has no case covering eviction interacting with root-span presence.

adjudication.rationale: In `add-buffer.lua` the new size cap uses `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)` after storing spans in a sorted set keyed by `end_timestamp_precise` (`zadd` in `spans/buffer.py`). `zpopmin` evicts the *lowest score* entries, which can include the root/segment span payload itself. This creates a verifiable inconsistency introduced by the diff: the set can lose the root payload while the marker still indicates a root exists, enabling later processing to treat a segment as having a root when it does not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The redirect-follow loop limit is silently reduced from 10000 to 1000 with no comment, test, or migration note. adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` the redirect-follow loop bound is reduced from `for i = 0, 10000 do` (with an explanatory comment) to `for i = 0, 1000 do` with no equivalent comment or any handling of the “hit the limit” condition. The loop only terminates early via `break` when `hget` returns nil/self; if the chain is longer than 1000, the loop will fall off the end and proceed using a potentially non-final `set_span_id`, silently changing correctness for deep redirect chains.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The max_segment_spans guard (skip oversized segments by span count) is deleted with no replacement; the only remaining cap is the byte-size check, while the Lua-side 1000 cap only applies to the add-buffer path, not the process_spans zadd path. adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the span-count guard in `_load_segment_data` was removed: the block that checked `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`, emitted `segment_span_count_exceeded`, and dropped the segment is deleted, leaving only the byte-size check (`sizes[key] > self.max_segment_bytes`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The max_segment_spans check (span count cap, with its metric and log) is deleted from _load_segment_data and replaced only by the Lua-side zpopmin eviction cap of 1000, removing the Python-side enforcement of self.max_segment_spans. Any code path that populates the zset without going through add-buffer.lua (or a future writer bug) no longer trips the segment_span_count_exceeded guard; the flusher will attempt to process unboundedly large segments even though the config knob still exists, leaving a ships-inert setting and a lost invariant.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Python-side span-count cap in `_load_segment_data`: the block that checked `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` and emitted `segment_span_count_exceeded` is deleted and not replaced with any equivalent enforcement in Python. The new Lua eviction (`if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin ...`) is a fixed 1000-item cap and only applies when population flows through `add-buffer.lua`; meanwhile `SpansBuffer.process_spans` now writes directly to Redis via `p.zadd(...)`, which bypasses that Lua eviction entirely. As a result, `self.max_segment_spans` is no longer enforced on at least one concrete writer path shown in the diff, and oversized segments can be loaded/processed until only the byte-size guard triggers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The eviction cap of 1000 is hardcoded in Lua while the Python side already carries max_segment_spans / max_segment_bytes knobs, creating two independently maintained limits with no shared source of truth. The next person tuning max_segment_spans in options will see no effect because the real cap is the hardcoded 1000 in the Lua script; the two limits will drift and segments will be silently truncated to the Lua value.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes a span-count cap of 1000 in `add-buffer.lua` (`if span_count > 1000 then ... zpopmin ...`) while the Python buffer logic previously enforced a configurable span-count limit via `self.max_segment_spans` in `_load_segment_data` but that check is removed in this diff. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The negative-offset branch in OptimizedCursorPaginator claims 'Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', which is false — Django querysets raise ValueError for negative slice indices, so the advertised feature path crashes rather than paginating. Any admin hitting the endpoint with optimized_pagination=true and a cursor carrying a negative offset gets a 500 instead of results; also the removed redirect-loop-comment style of 'this is safe because...' comments asserts invariants the code does not hold.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds a negative-offset code path in `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`:

```py
if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0:
    start_offset = cursor.offset
    stop = start_offset + limit + extra
    results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])
```

This directly slices a Django `QuerySet` with a negative start index. Django QuerySets do not support negative slice indices and raise an exception, so any request that reaches this branch (enabled via `optimized_pagination=true` plus `enable_advanced_features=True` from the endpoint) with a cursor containing a negative `offset` will crash the endpoint (500) rather than paginate. The inline comment claiming the ORM “properly handles negative slicing automatically” is contradicted by Django behavior, making this a real defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Rolling deploy breaks: keys written by the old code as Redis SETs (via sadd/sunionstore) are now read with zcard/zadd/zunionstore, which fail with WRONGTYPE for non-sorted-set keys. During the deploy window, any trace whose span-buf:s / span-buf:sr keys were created by old code and still within their TTL makes the entire Lua script error on every ingest for that trace; the Kafka consumer's process_batch call fails and span ingestion stalls for those traces until the old keys expire.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Redis data structure used for span buffer keys from SETs to ZSETs: Python writes `span-buf:s:{...}` with `sadd` before, now `zadd` (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py), and reads with `sscan` before, now `zscan`. The Lua script similarly switches `scard`/`sunionstore` to `zcard`/`zunionstore` and does `zpopmin` trimming (src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua). There is no compatibility handling for existing keys created by old code as SETs while new code calls `zcard`/`zunionstore`/`zpopmin` on them; in Redis this will raise WRONGTYPE and abort the script. This supports the finding that a rolling deploy can break ingestion for traces whose keys still exist under the old type until TTL expiry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The zpopmin eviction is enforced only on the Lua-script write path, while the second write path in SpansBuffer.process_spans (buffer.py, p.zadd at the tree-processing branch) writes to the same set keys with no eviction or count cap. Segments that arrive via the Python pipeline path (segment trees buffered directly under span-buf:s: keys) grow unbounded in span count — the exact condition the eviction was added to prevent is only half-prevented, and the buffer's memory for those keys grows until set_timeout expiry.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a 1000-item cap via `zpopmin` only in `add-buffer.lua` after `zunionstore`/`zcard`, but `SpansBuffer.process_spans` now also writes to the same `span-buf:s:{...}:...` keys using `p.zadd(...)` with no analogous cap/eviction. Since `_load_segment_data` also removed the prior span-count guard (it no longer checks `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`), spans arriving through the Python pipeline path can cause those sorted sets to grow until TTL expiry, bypassing the Lua eviction entirely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The negative-offset 'advanced pagination' path passes a negative start to queryset[start_offset:stop], which Django cannot translate to SQL; Django evaluates negative-index slices by fetching the entire queryset into memory. Any request reaching OptimizedCursorPaginator with a negative cursor offset materializes the full audit-log table in Python (plus the count_hits query); for the 'high-volume audit log access patterns' this feature advertises, the endpoint OOMs or times out instead of returning a page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an explicit code path in `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` that, when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and executes `list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` (i.e., a negative-start slice). This is a real behavior change introduced by the diff and is very likely to break pagination or cause severe performance issues because Django QuerySet slicing is not designed for negative start offsets (it typically errors rather than generating a bounded SQL slice). Regardless of whether it OOMs vs raises, the advertised ‘negative offset’ feature is unsound as implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] zpopmin silently drops the oldest span payloads with no metric, no log, and a bare magic number 1000 whose unit is 'spans per segment' only by reading the eviction arithmetic. Operators lose span data in segments >1000 spans with zero observability — no dropped-span metric to alert on — and the 1000 limit is uncoordinated with max_segment_spans/segment_page_size, so the next editor tuning one limit will silently diverge from the other.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the new cap `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000) end` will actively remove span payloads from the Redis sorted set (dropping the lowest-score/oldest entries) with no accompanying metric/log in the script. This is verifiable silent data loss introduced by the diff. Additionally, the prior Python-side span-count guard in `_load_segment_data` (which emitted metrics/logs when `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`) was removed, so there is now no observable signal in this path when over-limit spans are discarded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] A raw query param `optimized_pagination=true` silently switches the endpoint between two paginator classes with different cursor encodings and result semantics, with no feature flag or options entry to disable it. adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new, undocumented behavior switch in `organization_auditlogs.get`: `optimized_pagination=true` (when `request.user.is_superuser` or `organization_context.member.has_global_access`) changes `paginator_cls` from `DateTimePaginator` to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and also passes `enable_advanced_features=True` (see the new conditional `use_optimized`/`enable_advanced`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result with the two divergences being the negative-offset branch and `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` still comparing against the raw (possibly negative) offset while stop was computed from start_offset. The next fix or change to pagination logic must be applied in two places and they have already drifted within this diff (the prev-page trim condition is wrong on the negative-offset path it was written for); maintainers of the shared paginator will miss the copy.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the negative-offset branch sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and `stop = start_offset + limit + extra`, but the prev-page trimming logic later still uses `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra:` where `offset` is the raw `cursor.offset` (possibly negative). adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the redirect-chain walk loop cap was changed from `for i = 0, 10000 do` (with an explanatory comment about correctness tradeoffs) to `for i = 0, 1000 do` with no fallback/handling if the chain exceeds the cap. Segments accumulated before the deploy (or via the un-evicted Python write path) with many small-but-under-byte-cap spans now flow into segment assembly unbounded in count, and the spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded metric consumers lose their signal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the span-count guard on the read/flush path in `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data`: the block that checked `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans: ... del payloads[key] ...` is deleted and not replaced (now it always `payloads[key].extend(...)` as it `zscan`s). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Reading end_timestamp_precise with a bare dict access `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` makes the field hard-required for every span event in the batch, though SpanEvent's other optional fields are read with .get. Any producer (older SDK-relay path or out-of-tree publisher) emitting ingest_spans_v1 without end_timestamp_precise raises KeyError and fails the whole process_batch for the entire Kafka batch, not just the one malformed message.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py`, the new field is read via bare dict access `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` after `val = rapidjson.loads(...)`.
